## Summary

ZTE was founded in 1985 as Zhongxing Semiconductor in Shenzhen by investors linked to China's Ministry of Aerospace Industry and is a partially state-owned company headquartered on Hi-tech Road South, Shenzhen [1]. It makes wireless, switching, optical and data telecom equipment and Axon, Nubia, RedMagic and Blade smartphones [1]. The IEEE registry lists 493 MA-L blocks to "zte corporation" at its Shenzhen R&D building address [2].

A MAC in these blocks may be a phone or, very often, operator customer equipment: WikiDevi lists ZTE wireless routers, DSL modems, fiber ONTs, LTE gateways, mobile hotspots and USB modems [1][3]. Documented silicon includes ZTE's own ZX2791xx SoCs with MediaTek Wi-Fi in the BE6800 Pro+ (802.11be at 2.4 and 5 GHz) and the ZXHN F6600P, a Broadcom BCM63138 in the ZXHN H389A and a Lantiq PSB 50800 in the ZXV10 H201L [3][4]. WikiDevi gives ZTE the FCC grantee codes Q78 and SRQ [3].

The ZTE Score phone sold by Cricket and MetroPCS could be accessed remotely with an easily obtained password, a 2012 US House Intelligence Committee report recommended that the government be barred from buying ZTE and Huawei equipment, the US Commerce Department banned exports to ZTE in April 2018 and lifted the ban in July after a June settlement, and the FCC designated ZTE a national security threat in June 2020 [1]. Randomization behaviour is not documented by the sources consulted; the FCC ID databases refused automated access from this session.
